## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities Anti-Money Laundering / Combating Terrorist Financing

## Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Guidance Note and Quarterly Suspicious Transaction Report Analysis

The  Commission  wishes  to  remind  licensed  corporations  ('LCs')  and  associated  entities ('AEs') that the revised Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Guidance Note ('Guidance Note') issued by the Commission on 27 October 2005 will come into effect on 30 April 2006.   The revised Guidance Note provides LCs and AEs with guidance on how to implement measures and procedures in line with the new set of anti-money laundering and anti-terrorist  financing  recommendations  and  best  practices  issued  by  the  Financial  Action Task Force on Money  Laundering and the International Organization of Securities Commissions.  LCs and AEs should take all necessary steps to ensure compliance with the revised Guidance Note after its effective date.

The Joint Financial Intelligence Unit ('JFIU') publishes a quarterly Suspicious Transaction Report Analysis (the 'Report').  The Report contains, among others, sanitised examples of actual money laundering cases and statistics on the number of suspicious transaction reports received  by  the  JFIU.    To  assist  securities  firms  in  detecting  and  reporting  suspicious transactions, the JFIU has highlighted in the Report for Q4 2005 two money laundering cases relating to the securities industry (see Feedback no. 74 and 75). The Report for Q4 2005 is enclosed  for  your  information 1 .    To  preserve  the  confidentiality  of  the  information,  you should restrict the circulation of the Report to the compliance officers.  Previous issues of the Report can be downloaded from the 'References' section of the JFIU's website ( http://www.info.gov.hk/police/jfiu/ ) which is accessible only by passwords provided by the JFIU. If your compliance officers do not yet have such passwords, they can apply to the JFIU by fax (2529-4013), e-mail ( jfiu@police.gov.hk ) or post (GPO Box 6555, Hong Kong).

1 This Report will not be posted on the SFC's website.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

26 April 2006 Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities page 2

Besides, the Report for Q4 2005 indicates that the number of suspicious transaction reports from the securities sector remains low.  In this regard, the Commission reminds LCs and AEs that  they  have  the  legal  and  regulatory  obligations  to  report  suspicious  transactions.    They should  be  vigilant  to  detect  accounts  and  transactions  which  may  be  related  to  money laundering and terrorist financing activities and promptly report any suspicious transactions to the JFIU.  Failure to make a suspicious transaction report may result in prosecution by the Police.

Should  you  have  any  queries  regarding  the  contents  of  this  circular,  please  contact  Ms Maggie Cheung at 2840-9455.
